title: Why Your Gaming Username Is a Bigger Privacy Risk Than Your Password
summary: You’ve probably spent hours crafting a password that looks like a cat walking across your keyboard—uppercase, lowercase, symbols, the works. But your gamertag? That’s just a funny name you thought up in thirty seconds. And you’ve used it everywhere. Steam, Xbox, Discord, maybe even that old forum from 2012. The uncomfortable truth is that a reused gaming handle can unravel your entire digital life faster than a weak password ever could. With over 3.32 billion people actively playing video games worldwide, an enormous chunk of the internet is walking around with an OSINT-friendly alias they’ve never thought to protect (Exploding Topics). Even more striking, 80% of internet users also game online, meaning most netizens carry a gaming profile packed with linkable data (OSINT Industries, 2026). Let’s pull back the curtain on why your username is the real skeleton key—and what you can do to fix it.
